$comment: The two Notion databases LifeYoda reads and writes. This file is the authority on their shape: /lifeyoda:setup creates them from it, /lifeyoda:doctor verifies an existing pair against it. Property names are fixed by templates/daily-plan-page.md and templates/daily-journal-page.md and are NOT configurable — the workflows address them by name. Notion property names and select options are case-sensitive.
createOrderReason: The two databases point at each other. Notion creates the reverse side of a relation automatically, so exactly one side may be declared. Daily Plan is created first without any relation; Daily Journal is created second carrying the relation, which makes Notion add the plan-side property named in synced_property_name. Declaring the relation on both sides produces two unrelated one-way relations instead of one linked pair.

dailyPlan.title: Daily Plan
dailyPlan.dateKeyNote: Rows are looked up and deduped by their title, never by the Date column.

Daily.note: The date key. One row per date.

Date.note: Stamped by Notion when the page is created and never written by this toolkit. A Date that disagrees with the title means the row was backfilled, which is a signal rather than an error.

Status.note: Planned on apply; Done or Partial on wrapup.

📝 Daily Journal.note: Not declared here. Notion adds it when Daily Journal is created.

pageIcon.note: One emoji picked at random per row. Never ✅ or 📓 — those belong to the journal.

Day.note: Must match the title of the Daily Plan row it links to.

Date.note: The day being journaled. Unlike the plan's Date this one is writable, and must be correct even when the journal is written late.

Focus Hours.note: Derived per focusHours.strategy. The derivation is always shown before writing.

Track Hours.note: How the day's Focus Hours split across horizon tracks. Written by wrapup from the worklog calendar, which carries a [project] tag on every block; the project maps to a track through the horizon's track.projects. A day that touched one track carries that track and the whole number. Left empty when no horizon config exists — the daily budget comparison is then simply not made.

Projects Touched.note: Left empty at creation. Options come from the user's own sources.projectMapping; the workflows only ever select an option that already exists and never invent one.

☑️ Daily Plan.note: A journal must never exist without its matching plan row.

pageIcon.note: ✅ when every planned checklist item is complete, 📓 when partial.
